The lowest common ancestors of these compounds, including the histamine-1 receptor antagonist category, indicate a shared pharmacological mechanism that could lead to similar metabolic interactions. The binding of Cloperastine to CYP2D6 is explicitly noted, and the presence of a similar binding interaction with Diphenhydramine further supports the possibility of a general mechanism of action. The integration of these pathways suggests that Triprolidine may also interact with CYP2D6 through a similar mechanism, potentially affecting drug metabolism.
